notes: This is the standout run. The agent chose Before_Update__c instead of After_Update__c specifically because TriggerActionFlow.cls only applies flow output field writes back to the record in before-contexts (applyFieldValuesDuringBefore) -- After-context flows can add errors but a field assignment like this Description write would silently be dropped. That's a correct, non-obvious read of the framework's actual runtime behavior that this eval's own expected_output got wrong (assumed After_Update__c). The eval's assertions were written loosely enough ('e.g. After_Update__c') to not falsely fail this. This nuance should be added explicitly to references/framework-overview.md so future runs don't have to rediscover it by reading TriggerActionFlow.cls from scratch.

notes: Two compounding problems. First, the XML format defects above mean these records would not deploy as-is. Second -- even setting that aside -- wiring the flow to After_Insert__c/After_Update__c is a functional regression: TriggerActionFlow.cls only writes flow output field values (like this Description assignment) back to the record in before-contexts; after-context flows can add errors but field writes are silently dropped. So even with valid XML, this conversion would run the flow on every insert/update but the Description would never actually get set -- a silent behavior change from the original working flow. The with_skill run avoided both problems.
